prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, in which many neutral atoms are trapped at a magic wavelength so that the lattice leaves the clock transition unshifted, reaching fractional uncertainties near 1e-18

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B041 alone, credited to Katori and Ye. Having read the whole first-round exchange, I think the chair's central question, which criterion should separate B018 from B041, has an answer I can state in scientific terms. The question is what was actually introduced into physics and whether the evidence for it is complete. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the trap-induced shift on a clock transition, which is the step that lets very many neutral atoms be interrogated in parallel. That is a different mechanism from the comb (counting optical cycles, 2005) and from single-ion control (2012), and the move from single-ion statistics to ensemble statistics, together with Ye's work on coherence and systematic control, is what produced stability and accuracy near 1e-18. Several laboratories (JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB, SYRTE and others) operate such clocks and intercompare them, and the claims are measured numbers that anyone can check. The credit is two names, the proposer of the scheme and the leading experimentalist, and I do not have to exclude a decisive contributor to fit the cap. Pending redefinition of the second does not change my view: the physics stands independently of that decision, and I would not tie a prize to a metrological committee's timetable. I could write the citation so that it is not read as a general metrology prize, and the wording above anchors it on the lattice and the magic wavelength.
statement.case_against: The honest case against B041 is that it overlaps in subject with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and that a reader could still call it a step in metrology rather than a discovery about nature; the committee needs a citation that makes the increment sharp, and I accept that this is a judgement and not a proof. B018 has the broadest opening support (all eight members ranked it, five in the top three) and arguably the larger conceptual reach across condensed matter, so declining to put it first requires an argument rather than a count. My own proximity to atomic physics may lead me to overweight how hard ensemble clock systematics and ultrastable lasers really are. Finally, the clock's most visible consequences (geodesy, redefinition of the second, tests of constants) are partly prospective.

responses.point: Moved B041 to the top of his list after dropping B020, but says that if the committee cannot write a convincing B041 citation that separates it from 2005 and 2012, B018 is the safer choice.
responses.response: I accept your test and think B041 passes it. The increment over 2012 is that interrogation of a large ensemble of neutral atoms becomes possible without a trap-induced shift on the clock transition, and that is exactly what the magic wavelength supplies; that is a different physical route from single trapped ions, not simply better control of the same one. The citation I propose names the lattice and the magic wavelength explicitly for that reason. I also welcome your conclusion that the comb and ion-clock contributions are best answered in the citation text and not by extending the name list. I would only add that I would not describe B018 as safer merely because the wording is harder: its difficulty is attribution, which no wording fully repairs, whereas the B041 difficulty is a question of how to phrase a clear scientific increment.

responses.point: Asks whether the decisive discovery in B041 is the lattice scheme or the later metrological performance, and holds that the conceptual step in topological classification is larger than an extension of precision metrology.
responses.response: I would answer that the two cannot be separated, and that this is a strength rather than a weakness. The lattice concept alone, without Lamb-Dicke trapping and control of shifts, would not have given 1e-18; the performance alone would not have been reachable without the magic-wavelength idea. Katori and Ye correspond to the two halves, which is why the credit is complete with two names. On scale, I accept your judgement that topological band theory has wider conceptual reach, and I do not dispute the quality of B018. I disagree that scale of reach is the criterion that should decide between two mature, reproduced achievements; the will asks for a discovery or invention of greatest benefit, and an invention that has moved a measurement frontier by two orders of magnitude and is used across continents fits that wording on its own terms.

responses.point: Moved to B018 after Eriksson's argument about interpretive maturity, and says the Kane, Mele and Molenkamp configuration is the one on which every opening ballot that ranked B018 converged, so the contested credit is the price of the candidacy.
responses.response: Convergence of ballots on one trio shows that the three names are the natural set within the cap, but it does not show that the history behind them is uncontested; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang proposed the HgTe structure that guided Molenkamp's experiment, and Zhang cannot now be recognised. I agree with you and with Eriksson that interpretive maturity should carry weight, and the same criterion favours B041, where there is no open interpretive question at all. I accept that a narrowly framed quantum spin Hall citation makes the omission principled, and I would support it as the prize if the committee decides that way, which is why B018 is my first alternative. But the argument you gave for moving from B030 to B018 applies at least as strongly to B041.

responses.point: Argues that the clock's largest consequences are partly prospective whereas topological insulators have already reorganised a field, while deferring to Kroll and me on the physics of B041 and being open to instrumental achievements deserving the prize.
responses.response: Thank you for the candour about distance from metrology. Concerning prospective consequences, I would separate the achievement from its use: the demonstrated results are already in hand, namely fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, independent reproduction, and routine comparison of clocks between laboratories, and they have already enabled tests of the constancy of constants and of gravitational redshift at centimetre height differences. Redefinition of the second would be a consequence, not the discovery. I agree with you that interpretation is the right test for maturity, and I would add that the clock result is a measured quantity whose interpretation is not in question. I take your point that B018 has reorganised how a community classifies band structures and I do not claim B041 has done something comparable; I claim it is a different kind of achievement of equal maturity.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the lattice clock sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 individual-quantum-system prizes, and whether the proposed citation wording is persuasive enough to carry that distinction.
Whether the committee treats a measurement invention and its performance as a discovery in the sense of the will, or gives precedence to a new class of matter as in B018.
Whether the omission of Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D work can be made principled enough by a narrow B018 citation, since if it can, B018 may rank above B041 on breadth of support.
My recollection of priority details of the first magic-wavelength proposal and early strontium lattice demonstrations is from memory and is not independently verified here.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with Katori or Ye is documented in my profile, and none is apparent after the first round; I have not collaborated with either. I do have documented collaborations with Anne L'Huillier and the Lund attosecond group, Ursula Keller's group at ETH Zurich, Luca Argenti and Marcus Dahlstrom, none of whom is a credited name on B041, B018 or B010. ETH Zurich is Wallraff's institution (B020), so I flag possible indirect proximity there, as before; B020 is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives and no specific recusal need is apparent.
